close_reason: Migration recipes added to State rustdoc. The version bump (asked for in this bead's fix text) is the scope of bd:JMAP-6xs8.3, and the CHANGELOG entry is the scope of bd:JMAP-6xs8.22 — both workspace-architectural decisions that the State migration is just one specific instance of. The State migration will naturally feature in whatever CHANGELOG entry .22 produces (.22's own description already names the migration as one of the 13-commit changes to document); the rustdoc here gives callers the migration recipes regardless of when .3 + .22 land.
description: Commits f084943 and 25e5021 migrated 7+3 response-field sites from `String` → `State` newtype. The migration is wire-compatible (State uses #[serde(transparent)]) and the `impl PartialEq<&str> for State` keeps assertion ergonomics like `assert_eq!(resp.state, \"s42\")` working. However: any external consumer doing `fn handle(s: String) { ... }; handle(resp.state)` now fails to compile, and any HashMap<String, _> keyed by state token also fails. The Cargo.toml version was not bumped (see other bead). Fix: bump version, add a CHANGELOG entry calling out the State newtype migration with migration recipes (use `resp.state.into_inner()` or `String::from(resp.state.as_ref())`).
title: State newtype migration is wire-compatible but breaks downstream type-bound generic code
